title: HE ASKED ABOUT EACH OTHER'S WELFARE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They
greeted each other and then went into the tent." - Ex 18:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at this greeting. Moses, the leader of a nation, the man who confronted
Pharaoh, goes out to meet his father-in-law, bows down, and kisses him.

Position had not changed how Moses treated the man who once employed him as a
shepherd. Jethro was still his elder, still worthy of honour, and Moses gave it
publicly.

That is a good test of what success has done to a person. Do they still bow to
the people who knew them before? Some of us become harder to reach as
responsibility grows. Moses did not.

Notice too that they simply greeted each other and went inside. Before any
business, before the reports and the counsel that follow, there is a personal
welcome. Relationship first, work afterwards.

That order is easily reversed. When we are busy, people become items on a list,
and even family visits get processed rather than enjoyed. Moses had a nation to
run and still made room for a proper welcome.

Paul's letters are full of warm personal greetings, names remembered, people
honoured. Romans 16 is almost entirely a list of people he cared about. That was
not filler. It was how he lived.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has increased responsibility made you harder to reach?
2. Do you greet people properly, or process them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me humble toward those who knew me before. Help me to give people my
attention rather than my efficiency. Amen.
